question.text: The length of a wire of a potentiometer is $100 \mathrm{~cm}$, and the e.m.f. of its standard cell is $\mathrm{E}$ volt. It is employed to measure the e.m.f of a battery whose internal resistance is $0.5 \Omega$. If the balance point is obtained at $\mathrm{l}=30$ $\mathrm{cm}$ from the positive end, the e.m.f. of the battery is

options.text: $\frac{30(\mathrm{E}-0.5 \mathrm{i})}{100}$, where $\mathrm{i}$ is the current in the potentiometer wire
